faq.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Short answers about the new Nostr-only Obelisk.
faq.q1.question: What is Obelisk?
faq.q1.answer: Obelisk is an open-source, Discord-style group chat client that runs entirely on Nostr. There is no backend and no database — every message is a signed Nostr event published directly to the relays you choose. Groups are NIP-29 groups, DMs are encrypted Nostr DMs, and your account is a Nostr keypair.
faq.q2.question: Is there a server I have to sign up to?
faq.q2.answer: No. Obelisk is a frontend. There is no signup, no email, no password, and no Obelisk account. You log in with a Nostr key and the app talks straight to your configured relays — there is no Obelisk application backend or database. Messages live on relays. Obelisk operates two public relays; every other relay is controlled by its own operator.
faq.q3.question: What relays does Obelisk use?
faq.q3.answer: Whatever relays you tell it to. New installs currently include wss://public.obelisk.ar and wss://lacrypta-relay.obelisk.ar, both operated by Obelisk. You can add, remove, or replace relays from the relay rail. Every other relay is independent and controlled by its own operator.
faq.q4.question: Do I need an email or phone number?
faq.q4.answer: No. Obelisk has no signup form. You log in with a Nostr key — via a browser extension (NIP-07) or by pasting an nsec. NIP-46 bunker support is on the roadmap.
faq.q5.question: How are groups implemented?
faq.q5.answer: Obelisk uses NIP-29: relay-managed groups. Channels, members, admins, kicks and bans are all standard NIP-29 events that the relay enforces. Any NIP-29-compatible relay works. You can host your own relay, run a private one for your community, or use a public one.
faq.q6.question: Are my messages encrypted?
faq.q6.answer: Direct messages are end-to-end encrypted. Obelisk sends NIP-17 gift-wrapped messages by default, so relays cannot see who you are talking to, and you can switch a conversation back to NIP-04 if the other person's client needs it. Turn on post-quantum protection in settings and the message is sealed with a post-quantum envelope as well, whenever your signer and the other person both have post-quantum keys. Group messages are signed but public on the relay: anyone the relay lets in can read them, just like a Discord channel. Run a private relay if you need a closed group.
faq.q7.question: Can I self-host Obelisk?
faq.q7.answer: Yes — Obelisk is a Next.js app and 'hosting' it just means serving static-style HTML/JS. There's no database to manage and no backend service to run. Run it locally with `npm run dev`, ship it to any Node host, or expose it through a tunnel. We're working on a static-export build for one-click deployment to GitHub Pages, S3, or any static CDN.
faq.q8.question: How do I get a Nostr key?
faq.q8.answer: You can generate one in the login screen. If you want a standalone signer, install a NIP-07 browser extension like Alby or nos2x, or on mobile use Amber (Android) or nsec.app. Keep your nsec safe — it's your account, no one can recover it for you.
faq.q9.question: What about voice channels?
faq.q9.answer: Voice is on the roadmap. The previous voice implementation used a Socket.io signaling server, which doesn't fit a backend-free architecture — we're rebuilding it as P2P WebRTC with relay-based signaling so it stays pure Nostr.
faq.q10.question: Does Obelisk work on mobile?
faq.q10.answer: Yes. Obelisk is a responsive web app and works in any modern mobile browser. Pair it with a NIP-07-compatible signer (or a NIP-46 bunker, once shipped) for a smooth login. A dedicated PWA build is on the roadmap.

features.heading: Why Obelisk
features.subtitle: All the chat. None of the servers. Your keys, your relays, signed events.
features.nostrIdentity.title: Nostr login — your keys, your account
features.nostrIdentity.desc: Sign in with NIP-07 or your nsec. There is no Obelisk account to create. Your Nostr key is the account, everywhere.
features.realtimeChat.title: NIP-29 groups
features.realtimeChat.desc: Channels, members, admins, kicks and bans are all standard NIP-29 events on the relay. Open protocol, no proprietary format, no lock-in.
features.encryptedDMs.title: Encrypted DMs
features.encryptedDMs.desc: Direct messages are end-to-end encrypted Nostr DMs, gift-wrapped with NIP-17 by default and NIP-04 when a conversation needs it. Only you and the recipient can read them.
features.voice.title: P2P voice channels over Nostr
features.voice.desc: Talk to anyone in a channel with no media server in the middle. Voice is WebRTC peer-to-peer; signaling rides on Nostr events, just like every other message.
features.selfHosted.title: No backend, no database
features.selfHosted.desc: Obelisk is a frontend. There is no Postgres, no Socket.io server, no auth service. Every message is a signed event sent straight to a relay.
features.spamResistant.title: Static-site self-hosting
features.spamResistant.desc: Self-hosting means serving HTML and JS. No database to operate, no Docker required. Run it from your laptop, a tunnel, or a static host.
features.zaps.title: Bitcoin zaps in chat
features.zaps.desc: Send sats from any message via NIP-57 zaps and Nostr Wallet Connect (NIP-47). No custodian, no platform fee, no middleman.
features.games.title: Games on the relay
features.games.desc: Chain Reaction, Vesta and Stacker run inside a channel with no game server. Every move is a signed event, and every client replays the same log to the same board.
features.adminCli.title: Open source
features.adminCli.desc: MIT-licensed, every line on GitHub. Read it, fork it, audit it, run it. The whole app is the client you can see.
steps.heading: Three steps
steps.subtitle: No signup forms. No email verification. Just keys and relays.
steps.1.title: Sign in with Nostr
steps.1.desc: Use a NIP-07 extension or paste an nsec. No signup forms, no email, no password.
steps.2.title: Pick a relay
steps.2.desc: The default groups relay is preloaded. Add any NIP-29 relay you like — each one becomes its own 'server' in the rail.
steps.3.title: Chat
steps.3.desc: Join NIP-29 groups, post messages, react, reply, DM. Every action is a signed Nostr event going straight to the relay.

pqc.heading: Post-quantum messages
pqc.subtitle: Encrypted messages sent today can be recorded now and read years from now, once a quantum computer breaks the key exchange Nostr relies on. It is the one part of the problem that can be fixed in advance.
pqc.status: Live in Obelisk. Direct messages are gift-wrapped by default, and carry a post-quantum seal once you turn post-quantum protection on and your signer and the other person both have post-quantum keys. The keys themselves live in the Nostr WoT extension and the @nostr-wot/pq library.
pqc.nostrwot.desc: Identity, signer and post-quantum keys derived from a single 24-word recovery phrase.
pqc.quantakrypto.desc: Applied post-quantum cryptography: design, specification and cryptographic review.
pqc.guide: Read the guide: making your DMs quantum-safe
pq.level.quantumDetail: Your messages are locked, and nobody can see who you are talking to. Even a future quantum computer could not open them.
pq.level.wrappedDetail: Your messages are locked, and nobody can see who you are talking to. One day a quantum computer could open them, though.
pq.level.basicDetail: Your messages are locked, but the servers that carry them can see who you are talking to.
pq.markNoGiftwrap: Who you talk to is visible
pq.markNoGiftwrapDetail: The servers that carried this message could see who you were talking to.
pq.markNoPqDetail: This message is locked today, but someone could save it now and open it years from now, once quantum computers arrive.

desktop.channel.sfuHelp: Adds a {tag} tag. Same join surface as voice, but the channel signals to operators “expect a big room”. An authorized SFU joins and forwards everyone’s media so the room scales past the 8-peer mesh ceiling.
desktop.sfu.help: Enter one SFU URL. Obelisk verifies its {info} descriptor and stores the returned identity automatically. Calls authenticate directly to the SFU; Nostr relays are only a compatibility fallback.
desktop.sfu.verifyHelp: The SFU checks your signed Nostr identity and whitelist when you join. The full pubkey above is available for advanced verification.
desktop.channel.forumHelp: Adds a {tag} tag (the wire value keeps its original name). The channel renders as a feed of publications instead of a chat stream — each publication is its own channel, with its own conversation.

features.meta.title: Features — Nostr group chat, video calls, games, stickers, and mobile PWA
features.meta.description: Explore Obelisk features: NIP-29 groups, voice messages, sticker packs, relay-native multiplayer games, mobile PWA, P2P video, large SFU calls, and portable Nostr profiles.
features.meta.ogTitle: Obelisk Features — relay-native group chat and calls
features.meta.ogDescription: Relay-native groups, voice messages, sticker packs, multiplayer games, mobile PWA, P2P video, large calls, and portable Nostr profiles.
features.meta.twitterTitle: Obelisk Features — Nostr group chat, calls, stickers, and PWA
features.meta.twitterDescription: Explore relay-native groups, voice messages, stickers, games, mobile PWA, P2P video, SFU calls, and portable Nostr profiles.
features.headline: Discord-style community chat.
features.subhead: Your Nostr key is your account. The browser talks directly to relays—no email, password, chat backend, or platform database.
features.ctaTitle: Bring your keys. Keep your identity.
features.ctaBody: Join the public relay or point Obelisk at another NIP-29 community.
features.item.groups.title: Nostr relay-based groups
features.item.groups.description: Servers, channels, membership, moderation, messages, and reactions are NIP-29 events. Obelisk has no chat backend or private database between you and the relay.
features.item.groups.alt: Obelisk NIP-29 group chat with channels and member list on desktop
features.item.voiceMessages.title: Voice messages
features.item.voiceMessages.description: Record and send voice notes from the composer. Audio is uploaded to Blossom and delivered as a signed Nostr message with its duration intact.
features.item.voiceMessages.alt: Obelisk desktop message composer where voice notes can be recorded
features.item.stickers.title: Sticker marketplace
features.item.stickers.description: Discover media packs, keep favorites, create personal stickers, and let relay operators publish server-wide emoji, GIF, and sticker collections.
features.item.stickers.alt: Obelisk desktop sticker, emoji, and GIF marketplace
features.item.games.title: Games in the channel
features.item.games.description: Chain Reaction, Vesta and Stacker run inside a channel with no game server: every move is a signed Nostr event and every client replays the same log to the same board. Turn clocks, seats and results all come out of that log.
features.item.games.alt: Three Obelisk games running on a Nostr relay: a Chain Reaction board, a Vesta island, and a Stacker well
features.item.pwa.title: Mobile PWA
features.item.pwa.description: Install Obelisk from the browser and use the complete responsive app: relays, channels, DMs, profiles, notifications, and calls.
features.item.pwa.alt: Obelisk mobile PWA showing login, channels, a video call, and a Nostr profile
features.item.p2p.title: Peer-to-peer video calls
features.item.p2p.description: Small voice channels connect browsers directly with WebRTC for audio, camera, and screen sharing. Nostr carries the signaling; media stays peer to peer.
features.item.p2p.alt: Obelisk voice and video channel on desktop
features.item.sfu.title: Big calls with SFU
features.item.sfu.description: Large rooms switch to a mediasoup SFU advertised by the channel. Choose which SFU server to use or host your own. Media remains DTLS-SRTP transport encrypted while avoiding a full mesh between every participant.
features.item.sfu.alt: Large Obelisk voice channel using a mediasoup SFU on desktop
features.item.profiles.title: Nostr profile explorer
features.item.profiles.description: Open any member’s portable kind-0 identity, follow them, inspect their NIP-05 name, and start a DM without creating another account.
features.item.profiles.alt: Obelisk interface with portable Nostr profiles
